response.rationale: Repeated injection into hand veins with subsequent painless symmetric hand edema, sharp wrist cutoff, and biopsy showing small-vessel ectasia without true inflammation or autoantibodies favors an injection-related vascular/lymphatic injury (vasculopathy) rather than vasculitis, scleroderma, CRPS, endocarditis, or primary venous insufficiency.

rejected.why: Chronic venous insufficiency is too nonspecific and typically lower-extremity; it does not explain the bilateral hand-predominant, wrist-demarcated pattern in this IVDU context.
Negative ANA/ENA/RF, absence of Raynaud or skin thickening, and biopsy without collagenous fibrosis argue strongly against scleroderma.
Biopsy shows minimal perivascular lymphocytes and small-vessel ectasia, not vessel-wall inflammation or leukocytoclasis; no systemic vasculitis features are present.
CRPS is typically painful, often unilateral, and associated with autonomic/trophic changes; this presentation is painless and symmetric.
No fever, normal echocardiogram, and normal inflammatory/hepatic markers make infective endocarditis unlikely despite IVDU history.
